source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound. This is the challenge series where our rogue Goldilock is exploring Azeroth by unlocking one zone at a time. But each new zone can only be rolled once a WoW token is earned. And we started this journey in Elwin. And so far we've completed Elwin, Red Ridge, Burning Steps, Swamposauros, Westfall, Duskwood, Searing Gorge, and last episode we unlocked Stranglethorn Veil, which is a zone that is absolutely chalk full of gold farm to test out. And well, we've already checked a few off the list, but the gold tally so far is only sitting at 79,000 gold. And with a token hovering around 300,000 gold, well, there is some work for goalie to do this week. And to start off, we have focused a lot on Northern Stranglethorn so far. But believe it or not, the farms aren't done here. So, let's make sure we get a good full clear of it. And up far north, there are a few more noteworthy things. First and foremost, I'm sure you may be familiar with Hemet Nessing and the base camp. And in current retail, well, he's technically gone off to fight bigger batter prey, but the nesting base camp is certainly still in effect with a few extra hired guns. But luckily, Hammet Nessing Jr. is still kicking around with quest lines to kill pretty much all of the beasts in the zone. And I'm sure the skins are worth okay gold.

source.quote: So, for old time sakes, I'm going to go ahead and work through the nesting quests for fun. But there is more to the base camp because we also have Jacalina Domet, a superior axe crafter, and she sells a few nice axes. First up, the Crescent Axe, which pretty basic look and a decent market value. Then there's Franciscaca, which likewise has a decent value, somewhere between 500 to,500 gold if a sale comes through. Then there's Bova, a two-handed axe with another 500 gold market value, and the great axe with a market value of around 650 gold. Now, I will grab a copy of each of these to hopefully flip them on my Transmon character, but these aren't necessarily unique appearances or particularly valuable. So, I'm not going to hold my breath or say it's a crazy find. But, we also have some cool soulbound home decor here for Goldie's house, which looks actually pretty cool. It's only 450 gold. It's a nesting mounted elkhead.

source.quote: Quite the prize trophy. And I'll happily part with the 450 gold to put this up in Goldie's home, though, it is soulbound, so we're not exactly flipping this. Anyways, with the base camp set, let's get after some goblins. And not necessarily the gold goblin type. I'm talking venture co- miners, which I guess since they're mining are technically gold goblins as well, but these ones only spawn in a very specific area up here in the north. And they are pretty tightly packed with a couple variants in there. But that usually means forest spawn farming. The only thing, these guys are not on the forest spawn, which means their loot is a lot harder to target because every time you kill them, you have to wait for a respawn. And they do drop a valuable item, the Goblin Power Shovel, which not only has a cool name, but it also has a market value between 25,000 and 40,000 gold and a pretty low drop rate of 0.4% from the strip miners. But since it can't be AoE farmed by a bunch of bots, it makes competition for farming this item a lot less likely for Goldie. So, what I'll do on Goldie is clear these guys out and kill some time by farming the blood scalp mystics in the ruins just above these miners because I'm still trying to get that pressed robe that hasn't dropped yet. And then pop back down every 6 minutes or so to take a few more kills in the goblins.

source.quote: And there are a variety of herbs available here. and strangle thorn and veil. And there doesn't seem to be too big of a difference between the north and the south. However, the shores and underwater areas do have strangle kelp, which may actually be worth targeting eventually because it is the most expensive herb in the zone, coming in around 20 gold each. That being said, it can be pretty tough to actually get because you have to swim underwater and dismount, which increases the time between nodes by quite a bit. Otherwise, the zone has a plethora of herbs like king's blood, liferoot, and bruiseeed, and a few other herbs that tend to float between the 10 to 12 gold range. And to actually fully gather these herbs in Strangle Thorn Veil without getting scraps and just pedals, we do need at least 150 classic herbalism skill, which isn't too bad to get. Only about 40 minutes of herb farming to get. But now that we're here, let's go ahead and do a dedicated herb only hour to see where it stacks up. And this is also good data to optimize a future dual gathering route. And I do remember from the mining only route that the south had some really solid iron ore, but not enough to warrant just staying down there for mining only. But perhaps if the herbs are good, too, it could be worth a shot for dual gathering. But that's for down the road.

source.quote: But I suppose that begs the question, doesn't it? Can dual gathering beat out herbalism only? Well, I for one am pretty curious. So, let's run it back. And since the cape, the south of Stranglethorn had the highest ratio of iron, gold, and silver, I'm just going to do a route in the south to see if the density while dual gathering is high enough to warrant only doing the southern cape for gold per hour. Because technically, as long as we beat out the herbalism only rate of 5,850 gold per hour, it would be an improvement and worth running the dual gathering. But I can already tell here while farming that the ore and herb density in the cape is super solid. And we're jumping between a lot of herbs and ores, which will hopefully mean the gold per hour is improved. And speaking of which, I actually noticed a little trick on Outlaw Rogue here for the strangle kelp in the oceans. We can of course use the grappling hook to get down onto the ocean floor to grab the herb, but also if I look up and cast grappling hook again on the surface of the water, it also pulls Goldie up and out of the water. So, the strangle kelp is definitely worth it with a double charge of grapplers up because our downtime is pretty low. Pretty much no swimming. But enough of that. How does the gold per hour turn out? Well, in addition to a bunch of herbs, again, we got several hundred iron ore and a decent amount of gold and silver as well. The result, based on the current mint buyout auctions, 8,190 gold per hour dual gathering. Yep, we're getting back into some seriously decent gold per hour for Goldbound. Between this and Zel Garub Trash runs, which I have been working on optimizing lately as well, it's pretty solid. But something else that's solid. Let me grab tailoring to show you because in the background I've been working on an improvement to the classic Elwin crafted by Goldilock linen shirts. This time IRL. And I'm pretty particular when it comes to t-shirts. I pretty much wear the same snowwashed oversized t-shirts every single day. So with that in mind, I've been trying a bunch of samples for different manufacturers to get the right fit that I actually want to wear every day. And well, we finally did it. So, now available, the Crafted by Goldie Greetings Travelers TE's. So, check out the link in the description if you're interested in grabbing one. And if you do, I appreciate the support. But anyways, we should get after some in-game transmog targets. And one solid one right now is between the north and the south border at the Mizja Ruins. And here we're targeting the mosh brutes, some ogres. And luckily, these ones do hyperspawn alongside with the witch doctors that populate the ruins as well.

records.name: Fadeleaf milling trial
records.summary: 246 herbs→Emerald/Indigo,4419 gmin/4459 marketoutputs; reportedmargins 1400/1500,5.7/6.3 perherb. Spokenrawmarket 3300 contradicts 1500 profit; flag arithmetic.

source.file: 023 - I Tried Earning A WoW Token In Stranglethorn Vale - Goldbound 22.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/023 - I Tried Earning A WoW Token In Stranglethorn Vale - Goldbound 22.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Which is about 5 to 10 times higher than the rest of the mobs in the zone, which mostly are below. 04% drop rate for the hat. So, this is a really good spot to farm to stockpile the hat and the bat. Of course, as a solo farmer, I can't hyper spawn these like a group could, but I'm definitely plugging away here on this one. But so far, no hats and no bat. And one thing that I think might be worth it considering how many herbs we have right now, but also how many have access to is a little bit of an STV shuffle. So, I'm going to go ahead and head back to Elwin to grab an inscription and see what kind of profit could be made from milling pigments here. And while we get a lot of different herbs here in STV, there are four primary ones. So, let's see if milling them down is profitable. First up, fade leaf. And at the moment, based on the min buyout for all 246 of them, they would go for about 3,03 gold, but the steady market value is closer to 3,300 gold. So, let's get milling. And as for the milling process, I am going to calculate both min buyout rates and market value rates. And this should tell me if it's profitable in the immediate market, which can be quite variable, or if it's generally profitable long term. And it looks like from Fadeleaf, we're getting emerald pigments and indigo pigments. The indigos have a market value of around 32 gold, but a juicy min biote right now of 52. And the emerald pigment is sitting around 30 gold. And from milling them all, well, it seems to be pretty profitable. The net change for minyout value increased to 4,419 gold, about a 1,400 gold increase or 5.7 gold per herb. But that might be because indigo is so inflated at the moment, right? Well, kind of. But the emerald pigment is also trading below regular market value. So, if you run the numbers using average market value, once mil, the pigments are actually worth 4,459 gold and the profit is over 1,500 or 6.3 gold per herb. Really, really solid. And these are definitely getting listed. And onto the next king's blood. So I have 265 right now, which is worth 2,900 gold. And the min calculation on this one is going to be a bit cooked because, well, they're listed for three gold right now, which is way below market value. But milling these down does give some different pigments. We are looking at gold pigment worth 38 gold minimum buyout at the moment and a market value of about 18.5 gold and burnt pigment with a value between 9 and 12 gold. But since the min buyouts on golden pigments and king's blood are artificially skewed, they're showing a profit of 5,000 gold right now or 19.8 gold per herb. But that really isn't realistic. And based on market value, the profit is actually more like 193 gold total or 72 silver per herb. So, so far it seems like the indigo pigments are the real profitable ones at the moment. But we do have a few other herbs worth noting. Albeit we don't get nearly as many of them in bulk. So, there's Khadgar's Whisker, which right now is valued around 2,120 gold for 169 herbs.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/023 - I Tried Earning A WoW Token In Stranglethorn Vale - Goldbound 22.en-orig.txt
source.quote: And one thing I've been doing is optimizing the Zelgar trash runs. Although, I can't really do them right now because I did drop skinning for the STV shuffle. So, I'm mining and herbalism at the moment, but let me walk you through the optimized route. So, when entering, stay on your mount all the way till the first bridge. Then jump down to the left to get the pack of crocs and of course loot and skin. Then up to the left is Gub with his catch of the day. And then close to the right are our first two packs of bats. Now this route is optimized. So there are definitely some fish and some bats that we skip. But the first two packs are fair game. And once those bats are grabbed, it's a quick jump down to Tortune to of course loot and skin. Then up the bank to the next set of ancient bats. From here, it's best to mount up and make your way all the way to the first large troll for the large sack and elementium ore, and then all the way back down for the second troll. I don't bother going up to the terrace for the bats up there. It's just a waste of time and not gold per hour positive. And if you're a druid at this point, it may actually be best to use your moononglade teleport to get in and out. But as a rogue and wanting to do uncapped runs, resetting here would hit instance lockout and drop our ghoul per hour. So, I continue all the way past the cache of madness to the terrace with the first set of tigers. There are two packs here, so kill and skin them both. And then down and to the right is the hut with the master chef. And get the tigers on the right and the back of the hut and take the master's chef's groceries for the day. And shortly after around and to the right is another pack of tigers to kill and skin. Then all that's left to do is to beline to the massive pack of snakes and kill and skin them. From here, we're just getting out and running past the Hive Queen. But if you haven't killed her yet today, do so. Otherwise, if you've already tagged her today, skip and reset faster. It's back out to the front entrance of the instance for a quick reset. So, what's the gold per hour on this? Well, initially on unoptimized trash runs, I was getting 12,000 gold per hour, give or take, from initial full clears, but this was doing all of the bats and all of the fish in the rivers. And with this optimized route, we can reset more often and pull in 14 to 18,000 gold per hour. The range is pretty big because after last episode, the tiger and the bat leather have dropped pretty hard. So, it's pretty variable at the moment how much gold you'll actually get. But, I mean, come on, 14 to 18,000 gold is crazy gold per hour for these zones. And if the only goal of Goldbound was speedr runninging the token, well, I would just camp here and do this for 20 hours. But, of course, we do want to explore the entire zone. And so to help visualize that, I've actually been running an add-on called zone timer. It has a little heads-up display showing my non AFK/play time in the current zone, plus the looted gold from mobs in that zone. Then with the zone timer tally plugin, it shows all of the zones. And I think this is super cool. So right now, Stranglethorn Veil is broken down into Northern Stranglethorn with 17 hours and 39 minutes logged so far and 192 gold of currency looted. Then Zurub, which tracks separately as a dungeon, and 9 hours and 12 minutes played with 937 gold looted. We did a lot of optimizing here. And then the Cape South Stranglethorn with 8 hours and 36 minutes played and 277 raw gold looted.
